newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Weak amid losses in crude values.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Weak amid losses in crude values.

text.p: Sentiment in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was weak on Wednesday in line with overnight drop in crude values and traders expected a slight downtrend in the near term.
Buying interest was thin, with an offer for the 180-cst grade heard coming down to $102.50 per tonne from Tuesday's $103.00 offered level, but there was no buyer.
Traders said 2-3 cargoes from the Mediterranean were heading east and should arrive in Singapore in the second half of June, slightly easing tight supplies during the summer season.
Exports from the Middle East were seasonally down because of increased demand for air-conditioning there.
"The overall sentiment is weaker than in the past two weeks," said one trader, noting a lack of fresh buying support.
On the demand side, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) issued a tender to buy two 0.5-percent sulphur fuel oil cargoes for July deliveries.
The tender will close on June 4 and is valid for two days.
Also on Wednesday, CPC said it had sold a third 30,000-tonne cargo of 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil at around $100 per tonne for June 9-18 on a free-on-board (fob) Kaohsiung basis.
"The price is not very good, so we only awarded one cargo," the source said. CPC initially planned to sell two cargoes.
Fuel oil swaps edged down also to reflect falls in crude values, with June swaps last quoted at $99.50/$100.00 against Tuesday's $99.75/$100.50.
On SIMEX fuel oil futures contract, June was bid/offered at $99.50/$100.00 and July was traded 50 cents down to $99.00.
The sluggish sentiment in the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market continued, with the market expecting results of an import tender by the Korean Electric Power Company (KEPCO).
KEPCO seeks to buy one 500,000-barrel cargo of 0.3-percent LSWR for July 18-22delivery. The tender closes on June 5
